intro: While the overall San Antonio market cooled a little this year, the city's top neighborhoods held their value, and several rose. Here's where the top of the market is, by the numbers.

sections.h2: The top addresses, by typical home value
items: Hill Country Village: about $1,269,000, up 2.1% in a year
after: For comparison, the San Antonio metro as a whole was down about 1.9% over the same year. Typical home values are the Zillow Home Value Index for August 2026, not sale prices. A specific home can sell well above or below its area's typical value.

sections.h2: Why the close-in neighborhoods hold up
items: Alamo Heights, Olmos Park and Terrell Hills: Alamo Heights ISD, with a 0.9572% school tax rate, the lowest of the area districts we track
The Dominion: gated, with estate lots on the far northwest side
Hill Country Village and Shavano Park: small cities with larger lots, minutes from the north side
Loan: above $832,750 (the 2026 conforming limit), most buyers need a jumbo loan with stricter down payment and credit rules

Taxes: on a $1 million home inside San Antonio, combined rates of about 2.2% to 2.3% mean roughly $22,000 or more a year before exemptions. Alamo Heights, Olmos Park and Terrell Hills are their own cities, so their rates differ
Off-market: many top homes trade privately before they ever hit the MLS. Ask your agent who is quietly selling

sections.h2: Selling at the top of the market
items: Pricing: there are fewer recent sales to compare at this level, so pricing takes judgment, not just a computer estimate
Presentation: professional photos, video and staging are expected
Patience: with metro homes averaging 88 days on market, a well-priced luxury home still beats an overpriced one every time

faq.q: What are the most expensive neighborhoods in San Antonio?
faq.a: By typical home value in August 2026: Hill Country Village (about $1.27 million), The Dominion (about $1.07 million), Shavano Park, Terrell Hills and Olmos Park (each about $910,000 to $930,000).

faq.q: Are San Antonio luxury home values going up?
faq.a: In the top neighborhoods, yes. The Dominion rose about 3.8% and Terrell Hills about 3.7% over the year to August 2026, while the overall metro dipped about 1.9%.

faq.q: Do I need a jumbo loan in San Antonio?
faq.a: Usually if you borrow more than $832,750, the 2026 conforming loan limit.
